text:
To Our Friend, Joshua Baer

Late Tuesday night, Joshua Baer, Co-Founder of @StationDC_HQ and Founder and CEO of @CapitalFactory, died in a private aircraft accident near Laredo, Texas.

Josh was 1 of 1. Everyone who knew him, or even briefly met him, would agree with that.

He'd walk into the Capitol wearing a Star Wars-themed Capital Factory graphic t-shirt, American flag shoes, his little dog Stormy by his side, and a Limitless pin clipped to his collar. Who does that?!

Josh was a friend, mentor, husband, and father to three kids who were his world. He was the ultimate connector, relentlessly optimistic, a technologist, and a believer in people before anyone else was.

Josh and I began formally working together about two years ago on STATION DC. We both had strong opinions, but we always saw eye-to-eye about the mission. Help entrepreneurs win. And we were both incredibly impatient about it - we couldn't, and wouldn't, wait around. We were going to build.

That impatience was never more obvious than the last time I saw him. He visited DC last week, and we spent a night catching up at STATION DC before dinner. For three hours (not hyperbole) he showed me every website, product, and agent he'd built with Claude. He even showed me how he was building a digital twin of Stormy: you could upload a video of her and the software would predict what she was saying to him. A Carnegie Mellon grad and a technologist through and through, he told me, "this is everything I've ever dreamed of! All the things we thought computers would be able to do actually can happen now! It's like magic!" His optimism, excitement, and love of technology were infectious. He meant it, and it rubbed off on a lot of people. He invited me to join him in Cabo that weekend to build a product that we both think should exist and could improve STATION's experience for our members - I couldn't make it, but we put it on the calendar for a few weeks out.

Not long before, we had what should've been a difficult, awkward conversation about the future - and he made it feel completely comfortable. He told me he was there for me, ready to support me however he could. Then he texted me a list of people he wanted to introduce me to. That was Josh.

He cared deeply about STATION DC - it became his gateway to DC. He and I both wanted it to be the front door for startups to win in this city. After every visit, he'd remind me how awesome DC is, how excited he was about what's happening here, and how much he loved being at the STATION DC Clubhouse with members. He'd tell me these early days genuinely reminded him of those first days in Austin 15 years ago - that something real was happening in DC and at STATION, and how intoxicating it was. You could feel he meant it. He loved seeing the city win. And it goes without saying that Capital Factory was everything to him. It was an extension of him - every piece of that place.

Josh was shamelessly himself. He loved what he did. He had a lot of fun. He played to win. He wanted to help everyone along the way - and he did. And maybe most importantly, he made a lot of people feel things, and believe in themselves, because they knew he was in their corner. That's a life well lived if you ask me.

We're going to keep building this thing - and keep believing in entrepreneurs, in the future, and in technology being used to help us. Josh poured himself into helping people, and the optimism, belief, and give-first approach he led with are how we intend to carry his legacy forward.

Take care, pal. I'll see you someday soon. Most likely as a hologram or something - that's probably what he'd want anyway.

text:
【6月18日 夜のニュースまとめ】
・Noam ShazeerがGoogleを退社しOpenAIへ移籍
・Midjourneyが初の医療ハードウェアを発表
・米政府がSK Telecom懸念でAnthropicに輸出規制
・金融大手の香港でのClaude遮断が拡大
・Unreal Engine 5.8がMCPサーバーを実験的サポート
・BigQueryの自律型エンベディング生成機能が一般提供
・リアルタイム視聴覚モデルMaineCoon登場
・KaggleポケカコンペでPrivate Sharingの懸念
・CMUの研究でCursor導入による生産性向上が実証

===

Noam ShazeerがGoogleを退社しOpenAIへ移籍

・Transformerの共同著者であり、Google DeepMindでGeminiの共同リーダーを務めていたNoam Shazeer氏がGoogleを退社し、OpenAIに移籍することが発表されました。
・OpenAIではアーキテクチャリサーチのリードに就任する予定であり、Sam Altman氏も歓迎の意を表明しています。
・GoogleにとってはGemini開発における大きな痛手となる一方、OpenAIのさらなる開発加速が期待され、今年最大のAI人材の移動として大きな話題を呼んでいます。

===

Midjourneyが初の医療ハードウェアを発表

・画像生成AIで知られるMidjourneyが、初のハードウェアプロジェクトとしてMidjourney Medicalを発表しました。
・全身を超音波でスキャンする機器を開発しており、MRIよりも安価で高速な医療スキャンを目指しています。
・2027年にはサンフランシスコにスパ施設をオープンする計画も明かされ、AI企業による予想外の医療・ヘルスケア分野への進出に驚きの声が上がっています。

===

米政府がSK Telecom懸念でAnthropicに輸出規制【続報】

・Anthropicのサイバーセキュリティモデル「Mythos」に関する続報です。
・ホワイトハウスが同モデルに対する輸出管理を課したことが報じられました。
・韓国の通信大手SK Telecomが同モデルへアクセスすることに対し、同社と中国との繋がりを懸念したことが背景にあるとされています。
・開発者からは、SK Telecomは中国の通信機器を使用していないとの指摘もあり、米政府の強硬な姿勢に波紋が広がっています。

===

金融大手の香港でのClaude遮断が拡大【続報】

・ウォール街の金融大手による香港でのClaude利用制限に関する続報です。
・Goldman Sachsに続き、JPMorgan Chaseなども香港の従業員によるClaudeへのアクセスを遮断したことが報じられました。
・米中間の地政学的な緊張が高まる中、コンプライアンスやセキュリティ上の懸念が背景にあるとみられます。
・金融業界におけるAIツールの利用制限が、地域によってさらに厳格化される動きとして注目されています。

===

Unreal Engine 5.8がMCPサーバーを実験的サポート

・本日リリースされたUnreal Engine 5.8において、MCPサーバーのサポートが実験的に追加されました。
・これにより、任意のAIエージェントをUnreal Engineのパイプラインやワークフローに直接接続することが可能になります。
・ゲーム開発におけるAIエージェントの活用が本格化する第一歩として、開発者から熱い視線が注がれています。

===

BigQueryの自律型エンベディング生成機能が一般提供

・Google CloudのBigQueryにおいて、自律型エンベディング生成機能が一般提供となりました。
・事前に設定しておくことで、特定の列が更新された際に自動でベクトル化し、別の列に追加してくれるようになります。
・設定や利用はすべてSQL文で完結するため、AI関数を用いたセマンティック検索などが容易に実装できると好評です。

===

リアルタイム視聴覚モデルMaineCoon登場

・Catnip社が、リアルタイムインタラクティブな視聴覚モデル「MaineCoon」を発表しました。
・22Bパラメータのストリーミングモデルであり、AIキャラクターをレンダリングのために一時停止させることなく、リアルタイムで画面上に表示し続けることができます。
・従来のターン制の対話から、常に存在感のあるAIキャラクターとのインタラクションへと進化させる技術として注目されています。

===

KaggleポケカコンペでPrivate Sharingの懸念【続報】

・Kaggleで開催中のポケモンカードゲームAIコンペに関する続報です。
・参加者間でルールの範囲外となる情報共有（Private Sharing）の兆候が見られ、コミュニティ内で注意喚起が行われています。
・一方で、提出デッキが公開される仕様であることから、いっそPrivate Sharingを許可した方が面白いのではないかという意見も出ており、議論を呼んでいます。

===

CMUの研究でCursor導入による生産性向上が実証

・カーネギーメロン大学(CMU)の新たな研究により、AIコーディングエディタ「Cursor」の導入効果が実証されました。
・Cursorを導入した807のGitHubリポジトリと、導入していない類似リポジトリを比較した結果、導入後1ヶ月で明確な生産性の向上が確認されました。
・コーディングエージェントを正しく活用することで、開発のアウトプットに大きな差が生まれることがデータで裏付けられました。

Now they can train their shoots after doing leg press 😏 via AR. 

Thx to @roboflow and @claudeai I was able to run a vision model on iPad Pro. 

Claude opus 4.8 - no one shot - but precise detailed prompts (12x) to get a first demo. 

Calibration is king as always, buts it a good start. 🦾

Final setup needs: 

> projector from the ceiling / short distance 
> also possible with big LED screen or LED foil to avoid the player shadows and more brightness 
> AR shoals fixed on the wall to get an  accurate distance measuring between goal <> ball. 
> multicam tracking next 

Loading other models like golf, basketball etc on the fly would make it a perfect all round app. 

Works indoor / outdoor. 

Will check if I can push it on smart glasses 🤓 too.

text:
클로드 vs. 제미나이, AI 최고 강자는 누구인가?

1. 구글(Google) AI의 역사와 노벨상으로 증명된 과학적 위상
현재의 대형 언어 모델과 생성형 AI의 뿌리에는 구글의 압도적인 원천 기술이 자리 잡고 있습니다.

딥마인드 인수와 알파고
구글은 2014년 데미스 허사비스의 '딥마인드'를 인수했고, 2016년 알파고-이세돌 대국을 통해 전 세계에 인공지능의 시대를 알렸습니다.

인프라 통합과 트랜스포머(Transformer)
구글은 AI 개발의 표준이 된 '텐서플로우(TensorFlow)'를 오픈소스로 공개했으며, 엔비디아 의존도를 낮추기 위해 전용 AI 반도체인 TPU를 자체 개발했습니다. 특히 2017년 구글이 발표한 '트랜스포머' 논문은 현대 모든 생성형 AI(GPT, 클로드 등)의 기술적 근간이 되었습니다.

노벨상 석권
딥마인드의 단백질 구조 예측 AI인 '알파폴드(AlphaFold)' 시리즈는 2억 개 이상의 모델을 대중에게 무료 개방하여 바이오·신약 개발의 대혁명을 이끌었습니다. 이 공로로 데미스 허사비스는 2024년 노벨 화학상을 수상했으며, AI의 대부 제프리 힌튼 교수 역시 구글에서의 연구 성과를 바탕으로 2024년 노벨 물리학상을 거머쥐었습니다.

코드레드와 제미나이(Gemini)

• X投稿のいいね/リポスト/ビュー（特にAnthropic公式投稿は数千万ビュー規模）
• 主要テックメディア記事数と露出

なぜ話題：フロンティアモデルの公開直後に政府介入という異例の展開。エージェント用途（特に長時間コーディング・自律タスク）での実用性とガバナンス問題を象徴。

6月11日頃発表。Ona（旧Gitpod系）のセキュアで永続的なクラウド実行環境・オーケストレーション技術をCodex（コーディングエージェント）に統合。エージェントがセッションを超えて時間単位・日単位で動作し、顧客制御のサンドボックスで企業展開しやすくする狙い。

なぜ話題：モデル性能だけでなく「実行レイヤー・インフラ」が差別化要因になるというシフトを強く印象づけた。「モデルを買うより実行環境を買う」動きとして複数の議論で取り上げられている。AWS/Apple/Googleなども類似のagenticインフラを強化中。

なぜ話題：研究・科学発見領域での「本物の自律エージェント」実例として注目。オープンソースである点も大きい。

4. Meta Business Agentのグローバル展開・ビジネス統合（話題度: 48）
6月3日頃の本格発表以降、WhatsApp/Instagram/Messenger/DM上で顧客対応を24/7自動化するMeta Business Agentが注目継続。10億超のビジネススレッドを活用したパーソナライズと、迅速な企業導入が特徴。将来的には市場調査や運用業務への拡大も示唆され、収益化（サブスク含む）の一環として議論されている。

なぜ話題：消費者向けメッセージングプラットフォーム大規模展開の現実例。エージェントが「実験」から「業務インフラ」へ移行する象徴。

5. エージェント向けベンチマーク・コスト・インフラ議論（話題度: 42）
• Artificial AnalysisなどでFable 5の高コストが可視化され、長期エージェント実行時の経済性が課題に。
• NVIDIA Blackwellが「agents-per-watt」ベンチマークで注目。エージェント需要で古いH100のレンタル価格が上昇傾向という指摘も。
• 全体として「モデル単体」より効率・電力・観測可能性・コストの統合評価が重要視されている。

なぜ話題：プロダクション投入が増える中で、単なる性能デモから実運用メトリクスへのシフトが明確になった。

6. Portable Agent Skills / コンテキスト最適化・マルチエージェントの進展（話題度: 38）
オープンソースで「エージェント用スキルパック」（テスト駆動、アクセシビリティ、デプロイ、観測可能性など）が急成長。Claude Code/Codexなどで再利用可能なskillsをインストールして挙動を標準化する動き。コンテキスト圧縮ツール（例: headroom系）や「loop engineering」（信頼性ある反復ループ設計）の議論も活発。Framer 3.0 Agents、Exaリサーチエージェント、コーディング「ファクトリー」系製品も具体例として挙がった。[2] (https://t.co/iw80RIUXfB)

なぜ話題：プロンプト個別最適から「再利用可能なエージェント資産・ワークフロー」へのパラダイムシフトが体感レベルで進んでいる。

7. エージェントのセキュリティ・実行制御・ガバナンス（話題度: 32）
• AWS Agent-EvalKitなど体系的評価ツールの登場。
• Kaggleで「AI Agent Security: Multi-Step Tool Attacks」コンペ。
• https://t.co/7lGoTA1a3h（TryArcade）が$60M Series A調達（セキュアなaction layer / MCP runtime）。エージェントが実際に「行動」するための認可・監査・支払い制御がホット。[3] (https://t.co/N1rgmWs7tb)

なぜ話題：エージェントがツール使用・支払い・実世界行動を伴う段階で、信頼性・コンプライアンスがボトルネックとして表面化。

補足・全体トレンドの知見
• 共通の大きな流れ：2026年は「デモから本番インフラ」へ。シングルエージェントからマルチエージェントオーケストレーション、一時的実行から永続的・顧客制御環境、性能競争からコスト・安全性・再利用性の競争へ移行中。
• 資金・製品：TryArcade/Arcade関連資金調達や各種デザイン/動画/コード特化エージェントの小規模ローンチが散見。
• 日本語圏含めグローバルで「agentic workflowの実用化」と「ガバナンス」が同時進行で語られている。

データソースは主にX semantic/keyword検索（2026-06-09以降フィルタ）、ウェブ検索結果、主要メディア記事に基づく。スコアは相対的で、状況により変動する。より詳細な特定トピックがあれば深掘り可能

GLM-5.2 proves open-weight AI is no longer just chasing closed models on raw capability. It is attacking their weakest point: access sovereignty.

That is the real story. Fable may still lead some overall/proprietary rankings, but GLM-5.2 is now a serious open-weight frontier coding/agent model, has a 1M-token context window, is MIT-licensed, supports local deployment paths, and arrives right as Claude Fable 5 became unavailable after Anthropic said a U.S. government directive forced it to suspend access.

The factual armor first

Your post has a strong viral instinct, but these are the claims to tighten:

“OPEN SOURCE GLM BEATS FABLE” should become:

Open-weight GLM-5.2 beats or challenges Fable on specific developer/design arenas — while Fable still leads some broader rankings.

Artificial Analysis says GLM-5.2 is the leading open-weights model on its Intelligence Index, scoring 51, while its Claude Fable 5 page still lists Fable as #1 overall with a score around 65.

“Top spot on Design Arena” is useful, but say it precisely:

As of the latest Design Arena signal, GLM-5.2 was reported #1 with Elo 1360, ahead of the now-unavailable Fable 5.

The safer caveat: Design Arena is a crowdsourced design benchmark, and rankings can move quickly. The official Design Arena site describes itself as crowdsourced, powered by user votes; the reported GLM-5.2 Elo claim comes from Design Arena’s own social post/search result.

“It surpasses Claude Fable 5” should not be stated globally. On Code Arena WebDev, Claude Fable 5 is still listed #1 and GLM-5.2 Max #2; on Agent Arena, Claude Fable 5 is also still above GLM-5.2.

“Open source” should be handled carefully. The model card says GLM-5.2 has an MIT open-source license and open weights, but in AI discourse “open source” can be stricter than “weights are available.” The Open Source Initiative’s AI definition distinguishes architecture, parameters/weights, and inference code, so the hardest-to-attack phrase is “MIT open-weight model” unless you are specifically arguing under https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F’s license language.

“Run locally today” is true but needs a realism check. GLM-5.2 supports vLLM, SGLang, Transformers, and KTransformers; Hugging Face lists BF16 and FP8 model variants and 18 quantizations. But 744B total parameters / 40B active is not “laptop local.” It is local-first for serious infra teams, GPU clusters, high-end rented nodes, or optimized quantized serving.

BOOM: Open-Weight GLM-5.2 Challenges the Fabled FableThe closed-model moat is not gone.

a guy asked claude fable 5 to design a humanoid robot. it burned 1.4 million tokens over 2 hours and shipped it

then it spits out full ad campaigns. storyboards. 3d keyboard animations. car promo sites. juice packaging for a brand called pomo

unity studios charge 200k to ship a vertical slice of a game

fable 5 ships six of them before you finish your coffee

the people calling this "just a demo" are the same people who called chatgpt a toy in 2022

the next 24 months are going to separate everyone who adapted from everyone who didn't

text:
How I Built Safar With Figma Make, Figma Weavy, MCP, Supabase, Firecrawl, AWS Rekognition, Stripe, Canva, and GitHub

This document explains how I built Safar for the Figma hackathon.

It is written as a practical build story, not a technical code document. The goal is to show how I used Figma Make, Figma Weavy, clear product instructions, focused prompting, MCP-connected tools, Supabase, Firecrawl, AWS Rekognition, Stripe, Canva, GitHub, and continuous testing to move from idea to working product flow quickly.

I Started With a Clear Product Definition

Before building screens or connecting backend tools, I first defined what Safar needed to be.

Safar is a tourist e-visa eligibility checker and assisted application platform. It helps travelers check whether they can apply, understand which documents they need, upload those documents, pay transparently, and track application status in one place.

The early product rules kept the whole build focused:

Eligibility checking should work without login.
One account should manage multiple family members.
Every application should be reviewed by a real human before submission.
Fees should always be transparent: government fee, Safar service fee, and total.
Applicant, admin, and partner flows should stay separate.
Status should always use icon, color, and text, not color alone.
The product should feel calm, trustworthy, and simple because visa applications are high-stakes.

These rules became the foundation for the full app.

I Created the Guidelines First

The first major step was creating a guidelines.md document inside Figma Make.

I used it as the product and design rulebook for Safar. It included:

Product purpose
Brand colors
Typography
Layout rules
Card, button, input, progress bar, and status badge behavior
Mobile-first design rules
Navigation rules
Fee display rules
Applicant, admin, and partner role rules
Things that should never be changed

This helped Figma Make keep the design consistent across the app instead of creating random layouts for every screen.

The design direction was:

Deep green for trust
Warm gold as an accent
Warm off-white background
Inter font
Mobile-first layout around a 390px baseline
Clear cards, simple inputs, visible progress, and readable status badges

I did not treat the guidelines as a one-time file. I improved them through conversation first, then started asking Figma Make to build screens.

I Saved the Core Documents Before Building

Before starting the actual design and build, I saved the important planning documents in the project workspace so I could keep referring back to them.

These documents included:

Product guidelines
First Figma Make prompt
Build process notes
Security notes
Testing notes
Landing page copy
Video script
Data pipeline plan
Visual and video scene workflow notes

This helped me avoid losing context and made the workflow more structured. Whenever I needed to improve a screen or flow, I could refer back to the same product rules instead of explaining everything again from scratch.

I Used Supabase as the Backend Foundation

After the product flow and design direction were clear, I used Supabase as the backend foundation.

Supabase handled the core backend needs:

User authentication
Session restoration
Applicant, admin, and partner roles
Application records
Family member records
Document checklist storage
Private document file storage
Application status updates
Edge Functions for backend actions

The product needed separate flows for applicants, admins, and partners, so role-based access was important from the beginning.

Applicants could start or resume applications, upload documents, pay fees, track status, and view approved visa documents.

Admins could review applications, check uploaded documents, request changes, approve documents, upload visa outcomes, and update application status.

Partners had a limited dashboard where they could only see assigned applications and perform limited actions.

I Used Figma Make to Generate Supabase Table Prompts

One part that helped me move quickly was using Figma Make to prepare the Supabase database structure.

Instead of manually planning every table from scratch, I asked Figma Make to generate ready-to-use Supabase SQL prompts for the database tables.

Figma Make helped prepare the table structure for:

User profiles
Applications
Application members
Documents
Country requirements
Requirement reviews
Scrape logs
Roles and statuses

I then copied the generated SQL into Supabase and ran it there. The tables were created quickly, and I did not face schema bugs during that step.

This saved setup time and helped me move faster from idea to working product flow.

I Connected Supabase With MCP to Speed Up Backend Work

After the tables were ready, I connected Supabase through MCP-supported tooling so the AI-assisted workflow could help with backend implementation faster.

This made it easier to connect the frontend flow with backend actions.

Using Supabase MCP and connected tooling helped move faster on:

Authentication
Role-based routing
Application creation
Document upload flow
Payment flow connection
Application status updates
Edge Function setup
Admin and partner dashboard behavior

This was useful because I did not have to manually translate every product requirement into backend structure from scratch.

I Used Edge Functions for Server-Side Workflows

For backend workflows that should not run directly in the frontend, I used Supabase Edge Functions.

These supported important product actions such as:

Creating applications
Uploading documents
Starting payment checkout
Handling Stripe payment confirmation
Updating application status
Supporting admin actions
Connecting Firecrawl live data lookup

This helped keep sensitive work on the server side and kept the frontend cleaner.

I Built the Figma Make Prototype Section by Section

After the guidelines were ready, I started building the screens in Figma Make.

The homepage was built around a calm, trust-focused message. It included:

A clear hero section
Primary call-to-action
Animated nationality text concept
Destination country cards
Live fee display
Coming soon country chips
How-it-works section
Footer and bottom navigation

Then I moved into the eligibility flow:

Select nationality
Select destination
Select visa duration or travel details
Add traveler details
View eligibility result
Start application after login or sign-up

The key rule was that eligibility checking should not require login. That was repeated often because it was one of the most important product decisions.

I Created Consistent Visuals and Video Scenes With Figma Weavy

Alongside the product screens, I created consistent visual assets and video scenes for Safar. This helped make the hackathon submission feel more complete and visually connected.

I used Figma Weavy as part of the visual creation workflow. Inside that workflow, I used Google Imagen4 to create consistent and accurate images that matched the Safar product story and brand direction.

Before generating the visuals, I first created the character and scene direction in Claude. I used Claude to prepare:

Positive prompts for the characters
Negative prompts to avoid inconsistent or unwanted results
Character consistency notes
Scene-by-scene visual direction
Clear image style instructions

After that, I generated the character references and downloaded the strongest outputs. I then imported those references into Figma Weavy.

To keep the scenes consistent, I used Cedence Reference 2.0 through the reference loader. I attached the reference images with the prompts so the new scenes could follow the same character identity, style, and visual direction.

The process was:

Create character direction in Claude.
Write positive and negative prompts for consistency.
Generate strong reference images with Google Imagen4 inside Figma Weavy.
Download the best character references.
Import the references back into Figma Weavy.
Attach the references to scene prompts using Cedence Reference 2.0.
Convert the reference images into different scenes.
Combine the scenes in Canva.
Export the final visuals or video assets.
Upload the final assets to the website or submission materials.

This helped me avoid random visuals. Instead of generating every image from scratch, I reused reference-based prompting so the characters, mood, and visual story stayed consistent across scenes.

I Integrated Firecrawl for Live Visa Requirement Data

Firecrawl was added to support live visa requirement and fee lookup.

The goal was to avoid relying only on static visa information.

The flow was:

The frontend asks for eligibility or fee information.
The Supabase Edge Function checks cached data first.
If the data is missing or outdated, Firecrawl searches or scrapes official visa information sources.
The result is normalized into the format the app needs.
The data is cached for around 48 hours.
The UI can show whether the result came from live lookup or fallback data.

I also included an admin-facing live data toggle so Firecrawl usage could be paused or resumed to manage credits.

I Used AWS Rekognition for Identity Liveness Verification

To add a layer of identity confidence before the human review step, I integrated AWS Rekognition for face liveness detection.

The liveness check was triggered at the point of application submission to verify that a real person was submitting the application.

The flow was:

The applicant is prompted to complete a face liveness session before submission.
The frontend uses the AWS Amplify FaceLivenessDetector component to capture the session.
The session result is sent to a Supabase Edge Function for server-side verification.
AWS Rekognition returns a confidence score confirming whether the session was live.
If liveness is confirmed above the required threshold, the application moves forward.
If the check fails or the confidence is too low, the applicant is asked to retry.

This helped protect the platform from fraudulent or bot-submitted applications without adding significant friction to the genuine applicant experience.

I Used Stripe Sandbox for Payments

Stripe sandbox was used to build and test the payment flow safely before production.

The payment flow was designed around transparency:

User reviews the government fee.
User reviews the Safar service fee.
User sees the total.
User accepts the no-refund policy.
User is redirected to Stripe Checkout.
Stripe confirms payment.
The application status updates after successful payment.

Stripe Checkout was used instead of collecting card details directly in the app.

The Stripe webhook was connected through the backend so the application could still be marked as paid and submitted even if the browser redirect failed.

I Used GitHub as Part of the Build Environment
